approval.cost: No submission fee, listing fee, or revenue share is stated anywhere in the docs read
approval.trigger: For public distribution. Building and testing need no review: 'Register your integration on the Developer Portal to get your credentials and start testing. Use draft mode while you build and validate your integration. Submit for review when you want to make a public integration available to all Canva users.' What triggers review is choosing Public distribution and releasing it: 'For Canva Connect integrations, public review is required only for public integrations that will be surfaced in a marketplace for all platform users. Private integrations don't need public review.' The Quickstart likewise says a public app 'will need to be reviewed by Canva and meet the requirements outlined in the submission checklist'. How submission works: complete Release > App listing details (Text, Media, Links); on Release > Testing instructions, if the app uses credentials to authenticate users, provide login credentials and explanatory details for reviewers; on Release > App status, agree to the terms and Submit app for review. 'The app will be added to Canva's app review queue, and a Jira Service Desk (JSD) ticket will be created to track the progress of the submission.' While in the Submitted state the app can't be modified (you must cancel the submission to make changes). Private apps have no Canva review: 'the team's administrators are responsible for reviewing it' (team owner/admin, criteria at the team's discretion), but Private is only available on a Canva Enterprise plan and only to your own team. The docs do NOT state a numeric cap on how many external users can authorize a draft/unsubmitted integration. After a public app is approved, Canva automatically translates its user-facing strings for 25+ locales before release; that translation 'may take up to approximately three business days' (a post-approval step, not the review).
approval.wait: Not stated (no Canva-stated duration for the review itself; only the ~3-business-day post-approval translation is quantified)

blockers.detail: The audience is chosen at app creation and 'can't be changed later'. Picking Private locks you to your own Enterprise team; picking Public commits you to Canva's review before general distribution.
blockers.howToClear: Choose Public deliberately for any third-party product.
blockers.title: Public vs Private is a one-way door

blockers.detail: 'The scopes you request must already be set in your app's settings in the Developer Portal. You can't request any scopes you haven't set in your app's settings.' Changing your scope set is a portal configuration change, not something you can improvise at authorize time. And 'Scopes are not hierarchical. Specifying asset:write doesn't grant asset:read permissions. You must specify both in the scope string.'
blockers.howToClear: Register the complete read+write scope set in the portal before building the authorize URL.
blockers.title: Scopes must be pre-registered, and they are not hierarchical

blockers.detail: Each refresh token can only be used once; refreshing returns 'a new access token, the expiry time for the new token, and another refresh token'. Reusing an old one fails (invalid_grant: 'The provided authorization grant or refresh token is invalid, expired, revoked...').
blockers.howToClear: Persist the newest refresh token atomically on every refresh.
blockers.title: Refresh-token rotation trap

flavor.recommended: A Public app with the Canva REST APIs (Connect APIs) surface enabled, OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with PKCE (SHA-256)
flavor.why: Canva's developer platform has two distinct surfaces, and they use OAuth in opposite directions. (A) Connect APIs ('Canva for your platform' / REST APIs, the 'Outside Canva' surface): YOUR platform is the OAuth client and Canva is the provider; users grant your integration access to their Canva assets, designs, folders, brand templates, and comments. Historically this object was called an 'integration' (Developer Portal 'Your integrations'); in the current portal it is an 'app' (under 'Your apps') with the Outside Canva surface enabled: 'Go to Outside Canva and click Start integrating... Canva creates an auth client for your app.' (B) Apps SDK extensions ('Inside Canva'): apps running inside the Canva editor; if one needs a user to authenticate to an EXTERNAL platform, Canva's 'OAuth integration' feature reverses direction (Canva acts as the OAuth client against YOUR identity provider), which is not a way to call Canva's REST APIs. The Authentication docs state: 'the REST APIs use OAuth 2.0 with the Authorization Code flow with Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) using SHA-256', and the token endpoint 'can't be called from a user's web-browser client because it uses client authentication with client secrets. Requests must come from your app's backend.' There is no API-key or personal-access-token flavor for acting on other users' accounts (a separate SCIM token exists for Enterprise team provisioning, an admin tool).

humanMust: Create the app in the Developer Portal (name 18 characters or fewer; choose Public or Private under 'Who can use your app?'; accept the Developer Terms)
Enable the REST APIs surface (Outside Canva > Start integrating) and confirm the Canva REST APIs integration method is on
Note the Client ID and generate the client secret ('It isn't shown again')
Select scopes on the Configuration page and register redirect URL(s) under Outside Canva > Redirect URLs
(Public distribution) Complete the Release pages and Submit app for review
name: Canva
nuances: Redirect-URI defaulting quirk: if multiple redirect URLs are registered and the authorize request omits redirect_uri, 'the first redirect URL that's set in your app's settings is used by default'. Token introspection and revocation endpoints are also provided.

'The state parameter must not be used to store the code_verifier value.' The code_verifier (43-128 chars) 'must not be accessible by the user or their browser'. A refresh may optionally narrow scope: the refreshed token can have 'the same or smaller scope as the previous one'.
Access tokens 'may be up to 4 KB in size'. On generation of the secret: 'store the secret somewhere secure. It isn't shown again' (you can generate a new one if lost).

Account prerequisite noted in Canva's official blog: when creating an integration you are prompted to enable multi-factor authentication (MFA) on your Canva account; social sign-in users must first set a password, then set up MFA. If users authenticate with your app via a third-party platform, you must supply reviewers with documentation and test credentials via the submission ticket.
prerequisites: A Canva account for the Developer Portal (MFA prompted at integration creation)
A server-side backend for the token endpoint (browser calls are blocked)
The Public/Private audience decision made at creation (it cannot be changed)

steps.detail: 'Your apps' > 'Create an app': app name (18 characters or fewer); under 'Who can use your app?' choose Public or Private; accept the Developer Terms; Create app.
steps.title: Create the app (Public)

steps.detail: On the app's Outside Canva page, click 'Start integrating'; Canva creates an auth client and takes you to Configuration; confirm the Canva REST APIs integration method is turned on. Note the Client ID; click 'Generate secret' and store the client secret securely ('It isn't shown again'). Under Scopes, select the scopes your integration needs (e.g. design:content Read/Write, design:meta Read, asset Read/Write, brandtemplate:meta Read, profile Read), and under Redirect URLs add at least one authentication redirect URL.
steps.title: Enable REST APIs; get credentials; set scopes and redirect URLs

steps.detail: Build https://www.canva.com/api/oauth/authorize with code_challenge (S256 hash of a 43-128-character code_verifier), code_challenge_method=s256, scope (space-separated), response_type=code, client_id, state (recommended), and redirect_uri. The user reviews and approves access in Canva's prompt; Canva redirects back with code (and state; verify state matches and stop the flow if it doesn't).
steps.title: Send the user to the authorization URL (PKCE)

steps.detail: POST api.canva.com/rest/v1/oauth/token with grant_type=authorization_code, the code, the code_verifier, and redirect_uri if one was supplied, authenticating with Basic auth (Base64 of client_id:client_secret, recommended) or body parameters, from your backend only. The response contains access_token, refresh_token, token_type Bearer, expires_in (currently 4 hours, 14400), and scope.
steps.title: Exchange the code (backend only)

steps.detail: Call the REST APIs with the access token as Bearer. Refresh by POSTing to the same token endpoint with grant_type=refresh_token; each refresh token is single-use and returns another refresh token, so persist the newest one. A refresh may narrow scope (same or smaller).
steps.title: Call the APIs; refresh (rotation)

steps.detail: Complete Release > App listing details (Text, Media, Links); on Release > Testing instructions provide login credentials and explanatory details for reviewers if the app uses credentials; on Release > App status, agree to the terms and Submit app for review. 'The app will be added to Canva's app review queue, and a Jira Service Desk (JSD) ticket will be created.' The app is frozen while Submitted.
steps.title: (Public distribution) Submit for review

tagline: A public app on the Connect APIs surface: Authorization Code with mandatory PKCE, scopes pre-registered in the portal and not hierarchical, single-use rotating refresh tokens, and Canva review required before a public integration reaches all users.

time.active: ~15 min of portal setup + ~1-2 hrs of flow code
time.total: Unknown: review duration is not stated (post-approval translation may take approximately three business days)
